predecessors.name: Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic)
predecessors.text: the mainland kingdom, restored to Ferdinand on the Bourbon Restoration of 20 May 1815

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Naples (Bourbon)
predecessors.text: Sicily, where Ferdinand had kept his throne in exile

successors.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
successors.text: the whole of the former kingdom, annexed to the Kingdom of Sardinia and merged into the Kingdom of Italy proclaimed 17 March 1861

ledger.x: 1815: the Bourbons are restored to Naples and Sicily.
1816: the court moves to Palermo (infobox 'Palermo (1816-1817)'), going back to Naples in 1817 ('Naples (1817-1861)').
1816: the Kingdoms of Naples and Sicily become one, the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
1817: the seat returns to Naples (infobox 'Naples (1817-1861)'; the page does not give the move itself).
1860: the fighting for Sicily ends with the surrender at Milazzo on 1 August, and the crossing to the mainland follows.

1860: the Calabrian campaign ends with the surrender at Soveria Mannelli: 'On 30 August the Bourbon army... was disarmed in Soveria Mannelli and surrendered without a fight'; Naples was entered on 7 September.
1860: the mainland is annexed to Piedmont-Sardinia.
1861: Civitella del Tronto, 'the last organized centre of resistance', surrenders on 20 March 1861.
1861: the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies ends.

wars.name: Revolutions of 1820 (Neapolitan revolution and Austrian intervention)
wars.outcome: The king granted a constitution (13 July 1820); the Holy Alliance 'decided in October 1820 to intervene', an Austrian army was sent in February 1821 and entered Naples on 24 March 1821, and the Carbonari revolts collapsed.

wars.name: Sicilian revolution of 1848
wars.outcome: Sicily was an independent state from 12 January 1848 until the Bourbon army retook the island by force on 15 May 1849.

wars.name: Expedition of the Thousand
wars.outcome: Garibaldi landed at Marsala (11 May 1860), took Palermo (6 June), Milazzo (1 August), crossed to Calabria (19 August) and entered Naples (September); the plebiscite of 21 October confirmed the annexation to Piedmont-Sardinia.

wars.name: Siege of Gaeta (1860-1861)
wars.outcome: The siege 'started on 5 November 1860' (range 5-12 November); the capitulation was signed on 13 February 1861 and Civitella del Tronto surrendered on 20 March 1861, which ended the kingdom.

certainty.note: A kingdom with an established land frontier with the Papal States and the sea elsewhere; no page opened dates a survey, so this is the administrative frontier of the restored realm.
The front lines of Garibaldi's advance and the beleaguered fortresses are approximate.
